status: Conditional preparation only; no load connected or new measurement performed.
request: Owner asks how to perform a loaded test or known-good comparison after A-D zero volts and supply-label identification.
target: Detached Flextronics FA230LM1-00 / 341-0703-01 external brick, not router PCB. Pin correspondence from supply-label.json.
known_equipment: Fluke 111; Jesverty SPS-3010C source supply; historical small resistors/probe tips/hook clips. No suitable load resistor or mating power breakout availability confirmed.
question_pending: Whether owner has power resistors (exact ohms/watts), a DC electronic load (exact model), or an appropriate six-pin mating breakout/extension. Existing source supply is not treated as a current-sinking load.
qualification_before_connection: Identify actual power-resistor model/markings and confirm adequate free-air rating or manufacturer-specified heatsinking/derating; ordinary small signal resistors are not substitutes.

Identify a properly mating six-position connector/breakout with secure insulated terminations; do not assume a computer PSU cable has the same pinout. Verify each conductor assignment unpowered before use.
Reconfirm brick AC disconnected and DC plug detached from router, check for residual voltage before resistance/continuity checks, and record meter lead baseline for connection mapping.
Keep the 12 V return and PoE return separate. No connection to the Jesverty output, PC/programmer or router. Fluke remains COM/V in DC-voltage mode, not an across-output current measurement.
planned_stages: Record a fresh unloaded B-E voltage and A-D voltage after AC is applied, then disconnect AC.
With AC disconnected and residual voltage checked, attach only the qualified 47 ohm load across B-E. Apply AC and record B-E and A-D voltages. Disconnect AC before changes.

After removing AC and checking residual voltage, add the separate qualified 1 kohm load across D-A. Apply AC and record both voltages for a brief initial observation (about 15-30 seconds), then disconnect AC and let resistors cool.
limits: This is a proposed light-load diagnostic, not a manufacturer-specified minimum-load or full-power acceptance test. Approximately 0.262 A/3.22 W on 12.3 V and 0.0535 A/2.86 W on 53.5 V. Stable nominal rails would demonstrate operation at those small loads only. Persistent zero PoE output with steady 12 V would strengthen the supply/cable fault suspicion but does not substitute for the missing minimum-load specification. Keep hot resistors supported clear of combustible material and fingers; final wiring instructions depend on actual equipment.
alternative: Known-good supported supply comparison, or a service bench with suitable isolated/floating DC-load connections and verified connector mapping. Exact replacement compatibility must be established separately.

references.use: Power-resistor heating and ambient-temperature derating; actual selected parts still unconfirmed.
Use COM/V for voltage; current-input measurements across an output would short the circuit.
